dimensions.assessment: Affects the Forest Service, regional trail organizations, and visitors to the trail across three states.
dimensions.evidence: direct the Secretary of Agriculture to conduct a study on the feasibility of designating the Benton MacKaye Trail as a national scenic trail.

dimensions.assessment: The action is strictly a feasibility study and does not automatically designate the trail or change land use laws.
dimensions.evidence: complete and submit to Congress the feasibility study for designating the Benton MacKaye Trail as a national scenic trail.

dimensions.assessment: The source notes the trail can be maintained at minimal cost, but details no specific study budget.
dimensions.evidence: can be maintained at a minimal cost

dimensions.assessment: A focused, single-project amendment to the National Trails System Act to mandate a report to Congress.
dimensions.evidence: Section 5(c) of the National Trails System Act (16 U.S.C. 1244(c)) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: One-time study requirement to be completed not later than one year after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this paragraph, the Secretary of Agriculture... shall complete and submit to Congress the feasibility study

missing_information: Cost of conducting the feasibility study
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the Forest Service to conduct a feasibility study within one year regarding the designation of the 287-mile Benton MacKaye Trail as a national scenic trail.
